findings.note: Package-global test seam mutated without restore: TestTornTailWritePath sets `nanos = func() int64 { return 42 }` and never restores it, unlike the sibling `flock` seam in the same file which is saved to `orig` and restored. Every later test in the package then sees a frozen torn-fragment clock, which is order-dependent state; the suite happens to pass today and under -shuffle=on, but the asymmetry is a latent isolation bug (a future test that writes two torn fragments would collide on runs.jsonl-42). t.Cleanup(func(){ nanos = nowNanos }) would close it.

evidence.note: nanos overridden here; no restore anywhere in the file.
flock = orig shows the intended restore pattern that nanos does not follow.

findings.note: The export fail-closed guard is only one level deep. TestEverySnapshotFieldIsClassifiedForExport enumerates run.Snapshot's own fields, but two of the transforms it certifies are field-selective on nested types with no equivalent guard: redactor.allowedCmds rewrites only `argv` and `file_hashes` on each AllowedCmd (Env and any new field pass through verbatim), and the last_error transform blanks only GateError.Detail. A field added to run.AllowedCmd or run.GateError would therefore reach an evidence bundle unredacted with this suite green -- exactly the failure mode the test's own header comment says it exists to prevent.

evidence.note: reflect.VisibleFields(reflect.TypeOf(run.Snapshot{})) enumerates top-level fields only; it does not descend into AllowedCmd or GateError.
allowedCmds touches only cmd["argv"] and cmd["file_hashes"]; every other key of the marshalled AllowedCmd is emitted as-is.

findings.note: TestRunsJSONLSurvivesInterleavedWriters is titled and commented as proving runs.jsonl survives its two writers, but it only covers the clean-tail path. appendRow's torn-tail branch still does a read-then-f.Truncate(t.offset) under a flock that state.AppendJSONL never takes, so a row appended by the unlocked writer between readRows and the Truncate is discarded. No case in the test plants a torn fragment while concurrent writers are running, so the stated guarantee is broader than what is actually verified. (record.go itself is outside this shard; noting the coverage gap in the test that claims the property.)

evidence.note: The concurrency test starts from an empty runs.jsonl, so t.fragment is always nil and the Truncate branch is never reached concurrently.
f.Truncate(t.offset) is a read-modify-write against an offset computed before the lock-free writer may have appended.
